coverage_gaps: Need primary-source verification from 10-K/10-Q filings, annual reports, earnings transcripts, customer announcements, and capex plans before moving from node hypotheses to company-level ranking.
Need market-pricing checks: current market caps, revenue multiples, analyst coverage count, short interest, ownership concentration, and recent price moves for candidate suppliers.
Need non-U.S. public-company mapping for Japanese, Taiwanese, Korean, European, and Chinese suppliers in substrates, OSAT, optics, power components, and thermal management.
Need technical validation of whether specific optical and packaging bottlenecks are truly supply-limited versus merely demand-cyclical.
Need customer dependency checks to avoid false positives where a supplier mentions AI but has immaterial revenue exposure.
Need falsification plan for each node: monitor lead-time compression, capacity additions, customer insourcing, margin pressure, inventory build, failed qualification, or demand slowdown.

The supplied external search context states that qualification for a new supplier at a major transceiver manufacturer can take up to twenty-four months and that the commercial-grade supplier base for a precision substrate used in 800G/1.6T optical transceivers is fewer than six companies worldwide.

memory_update.text: AI should be decomposed as an infrastructure and supply-chain capacity theme, not only a model/GPU/software theme.
ABF substrates and advanced interconnect are a priority underfollowed node because AI accelerators depend on high-end substrates with concentrated suppliers and long capacity lead times.

Optical interconnect and photonics components are a priority underfollowed node because AI networking bandwidth demand may expose InP, laser, photodetector, optical substrate, and qualification bottlenecks.

Advanced packaging, HBM backend, and OSAT capacity should be tracked as a separate node because HBM demand may crowd out conventional memory backend work and increase demand for qualified outsourcing capacity.

Data-center power and thermal subcomponents are an underfollowed industrial discovery lane because AI rack density creates demand for switchgear, transformers, busway, liquid-cooling, pumps, cold plates, and thermal systems.

Layer 1B should build a candidate universe across U.S., Japan, Taiwan, Korea, Europe, and Canada, then attach market cap, analyst coverage, AI revenue evidence, customer concentration, and source quality.

layer1a.summary: Layer 1A decomposes AI as an infrastructure buildout rather than a single GPU trade. The highest-quality research lanes are where AI demand forces physical constraints: advanced packaging and substrates, optical interconnects and photonics materials, HBM and memory backend capacity, data-center power and thermal infrastructure, grid/nuclear power supply, and enterprise/industrial AI automation software. Reference leaders such as NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC, ASML, Arista, Vertiv, Eaton, Constellation, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta define demand, but the discovery mandate should deliberately search one or two layers upstream for underfollowed small/mid-cap suppliers, qualification bottlenecks, test/inspection vendors, materials providers, outsourced backend capacity, and niche software/data platforms. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: ABF substrate capacity remains a multi-year constraint for leading-edge AI chips because qualification is strict, capacity additions take roughly 18-24 months, and supply is concentrated among a small group of Asian substrate specialists.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize small/mid-cap and non-U.S. listed substrate suppliers with rising AI/HPC mix, lower consumer exposure, capex expansion, and signs of tight allocation. Also search for niche equipment/material suppliers below USD 10B market cap.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Photonics manufacturing capacity, especially InP-dependent devices and qualified precision substrates for 800G/1.6T optical transceivers, may be harder to expand quickly than market narratives imply because supplier qualification can take up to two years and the commercial-grade supplier base is small.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: As AI clusters scale, east-west traffic and GPU/accelerator interconnect bandwidth rise sharply. Optical links, high-speed transceivers, lasers, photodetectors, and photonic integration may become a gating factor for cluster deployment.

supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Look for listed OSAT/backend companies with AI/HPC customer validation, yield progress, price increases, capacity additions, or customer-backed technology transitions. Favor companies with measurable revenue mix change over story-only exposure.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Many AI software stories are crowded, but underfollowed vertical platforms with proprietary datasets, regulated workflows, embedded distribution, or implementation depth may benefit from enterprise AI adoption without being priced like obvious AI leaders.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: If AI infrastructure supply expands, value capture may shift toward software that turns model capability into measurable automation. The scarce layer may be trusted data, domain workflows, integrations, security, and customer-specific deployment capacity.

demand_drivers: Hyperscaler AI capex for training and inference clusters, including GPUs, custom ASICs, high-bandwidth memory, high-speed networking, and data-center campuses.

Shift from GPU-centric training toward hyperscaler-scale custom AI accelerators and AI networking, increasing demand for advanced packaging, substrates, Ethernet/switching silicon, optical links, and backend test capacity.

Rapid growth in AI data-center interconnect bandwidth requirements, moving from copper and conventional optics toward 800G, 1.6T, co-packaged optics, silicon photonics, InP lasers, photodetectors, and precision optical substrates.
Rising power density of AI servers, creating demand for electrical gear, cooling systems, liquid cooling, transformers, switchgear, grid interconnects, and reliable baseload or contracted power.

Enterprise and industrial automation adoption of AI software, where the bottleneck may be proprietary data integration, workflow embedding, regulated deployment, security, and domain-specific implementation rather than model access alone.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Use a two-lane funnel. Lane 1 maps reference leaders to understand demand signals, capex cycles, and technical requirements. Lane 2 searches for underfollowed public companies exposed to chokepoints: substrates, optical components, compound semiconductors, outsourced semiconductor assembly/test, advanced PCB/interconnect, thermal/power subcomponents, grid services, nuclear fuel/components, and vertical AI software/data vendors. Prefer public companies with market caps roughly USD 300M-10B where plausible; allow USD 10B-30B if exposure is unusually pure; label micro-caps as speculative. Avoid ranking securities at Layer 1A; instead produce nodes, search queries, and falsifiable hypotheses for later evidence collection.
supply_side_constraints: Advanced packaging capacity, including CoWoS-like capacity, fan-out panel-level packaging, HBM assembly, and high-yield test, has long lead times and may crowd out conventional memory/backend work.
ABF substrates and high-end interconnect materials are qualification-heavy, capacity-constrained, and concentrated among a small set of suppliers.

Optical transceiver supply chains depend on constrained photonics materials and components, including InP wafers/devices, lasers, photodetectors, optical substrates, and qualified manufacturing capacity.
Data-center electrical infrastructure is constrained by lead times in transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, power modules, grid interconnection, and skilled construction labor.
AI data-center power availability depends on utility interconnection queues, transmission buildout, natural gas turbine availability, nuclear restart/licensing, fuel supply, and regulatory approvals.
AI software deployment is constrained by customer data readiness, compliance, integration labor, security approvals, and measurable ROI proof.
